title: Dzowoe
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: Equal weights of groundnut paste and toasted corn flour with cayenne, ginger and clove — warrior food, by her account, needing no cooking at all.
longDesc: Dzowoe is a spiced peanut ball and it is one of the oldest-feeling foods in this collection: a hundred and fifty grams of groundnut paste to a hundred and fifty of toasted corn flour, with a tablespoon of cayenne, a tablespoon of ginger powder, half a teaspoon of clove powder, a tablespoon of sugar and optional salt. Nothing is cooked — the corn flour is already toasted and the paste binds it. Her note is that dzowoe was one of the few preparations prepared as seasoned food for warriors in battle, which makes sense: it keeps, it travels and it is dense with calories.
ingredients: 150 g toasted corn flour (tom brown flour)
1 tbsp cayenne pepper, or 1 tsp chilli powder
steps: // The published method for this recipe is video-only. No written steps exist in the source.
Combine the toasted corn flour with the cayenne, ginger powder, clove powder, sugar and optional salt.
Work in the groundnut paste until the mixture comes together.
Press and roll into firm balls.
// The order above follows the dry-then-wet logic of the ingredients, not this source's own steps.
chefTips: Equal weights of paste and toasted corn flour, a hundred and fifty grams each. That one-to-one ratio is the whole recipe.
No cooking at all. The corn flour is already toasted — this is the same ablemanu or tom brown that binds aprapransa and ayikple.
A tablespoon of cayenne for eight servings is substantial, and she notes this makes for a mildly spiced dzowoe. The traditional version is hotter.
Press firmly. Groundnut paste and dry flour will not hold unless you compact them.
Keeps well in a tin, which is why she records it as food for warriors on campaign.
The same snack is dakuwa among the Hausa of northern Nigeria, by her own note — a genuine cross-border food.
Be aware the method is reconstructed. She publishes a complete ingredient list and the steps are in her video.
commonMistakes: Not compacting the balls firmly enough.
Treating the reconstructed step order as the author's own.
Adding liquid, which it does not need.
Expecting it to be fiery — this version is deliberately mild.
sources: Quantities from 'The Ghanaian Spicy Peanut Balls (Adaakwa)', ndudu-by-fafa.blogspot.com, byline as printed 'Posted by Fafa Gilbert', Monday 1 October 2018. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS).

Ingredients exactly as printed: 150g of Groundnut paste; 150g of toasted corn flour (Tom Brown flour); 1 tablespoon of Cayenne pepper or 1 teaspoon of Chilli powder; 1 tablespoonful of Ginger powder; Half a teaspoon of salt (optional); Half a teaspoon of clove powder; 1 tablespoonful of Sugar.

METHOD GAP: THE METHOD IS VIDEO ONLY. No written steps and no cue. The steps above are explicitly marked as reconstructed from the dry-then-wet logic of the ingredient list, and the step list carries a header saying so. The reconstruction is low-risk here because nothing is cooked.
HER NOTE, as printed: 'makes for a mildly spiced Dzowoe' — so the cayenne quantity is her own moderation of a hotter traditional snack.

THE ORIGIN CLAIM, quoted: attributed to the Ewe, and 'Dzowoe was one of the few preparations our ancestors prepared as one of the seasoned food for warriors in battles'. That is her claim and is recorded as such rather than asserted as established history.
THE CROSS-BORDER NAME, as printed: the same snack is 'Dakuwa' among the Hausa in northern Nigeria. Note that this collection separately documents a Nigerian dakuwa, so the two traditions meet here.
NO YIELD is printed. The eight servings above is an editorial reading of 300 g of combined mixture.

THE TOASTED CORN FLOUR is the same product that binds aprapransa (GHA010, GHA093), ayikple (GHA046) and the kaaklo at GHA057, and that goes into tankora powder (GHA064). Its toasting is what makes it usable without cooking.

NO FERMENTATION and no cooking, so no cue is needed — which is why this entry is publishable from an ingredient list alone where several video-only recipes in this collection are flagged more heavily.
storage: Several weeks in an airtight tin.
healthBenefits: Groundnuts supply protein, niacin, folate, magnesium and vitamin E.
Toasted maize adds fibre and B vitamins.
Ginger and clove both carry documented antimicrobial compounds.
Very calorie-dense, which is why it travels well.
culturalNote: A dense, spiced, keeping food made of ground nuts and toasted grain is the kind of thing every travelling culture invents, and dzowoe being remembered as warriors' rations fits it exactly. That the Hausa make the same thing under the name dakuwa, hundreds of miles north, says how well the idea worked.
